# Initialization

```{r}
# packages
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(randomForest)
library(nnet)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(class)
```

# Importing and Processing Data

```{r}
# importing data
data <- read.csv("output.csv")

# adding majority vote column
data$highest_party <- apply(data[, c("DEMOCRAT", "REPUBLICAN")], 1, function(row) {
  if (all(is.na(row))) {
    NA  # or "Unknown", if you prefer
  } else {
    parties <- c("Democratic", "Republican")
    parties[which.max(row)]
  }
})

data$highest_party <- ifelse(data$highest_party == "Republican", 1, 0)


# adding total turnout column
data$total_turnout <- data$DEMOCRAT + data$REPUBLICAN + data$OTHER

data$dem_pct <- data$DEMOCRAT/data$total_turnout
data$rep_pct <- data$REPUBLICAN/data$total_turnout
data$oth_pct <- data$OTHER/data$total_turnout
data <- na.omit(data)
head(data)
```

# Model 1 - Logistic Regression

```{r}
# full model
log_model <- glm(highest_party ~ . - FIPS - STATE - ST_ABBR - COUNTY - LOCATION - POPCHANGE - dem_pct - oth_pct - rep_pct - DEMOCRAT - OTHER - REPUBLICAN - total_turnout - Male_percentage_estimate, data = data, family = binomial())

# backward stepwise
model1 <- step(log_model, direction = "backward", k = 2, trace = F)
summary(model1)
```

```{r}

```

# Model 2 - K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)

```{r}
### preprocessing
train_idx <- sample(1:nrow(data), 0.8 * nrow(data))
train_data <- data[train_idx, ]
test_data <- data[-train_idx, ]
y_train <- train_data$highest_party
y_test <- test_data$highest_party
X_train <- train_data[, -which(names(train_data) == "highest_party")]
X_test <- test_data[, -which(names(test_data) == "highest_party")]
X_train <- data.frame(lapply(X_train, function(x) as.numeric(as.factor(x))))
X_test <- data.frame(lapply(X_test, function(x) as.numeric(as.factor(x))))

### building model
knn_fit <- knn(train = X_train, test = X_test, cl = y_train, k = 5)

# confusion matrix
table(Predicted = knn_fit, Actual = y_test)
accuracy <- sum(knn_fit == y_test) / length(y_test)
cat("Accuracy:", accuracy)
```

# Model 3 - Random Forest

```{r}
data$highest_party <- as.factor(data$highest_party)

random_forest_model <- randomForest(highest_party ~ . - FIPS - STATE - ST_ABBR - COUNTY - LOCATION - POPCHANGE - dem_pct - oth_pct - rep_pct - DEMOCRAT - OTHER - REPUBLICAN - total_turnout - Male_percentage_estimate, data = data, ntree = 500, importance = TRUE)
print(random_forest_model)
```

# Model 4 - Support Vector Machine

```{r}
svm_fit <- svm(highest_party ~ . - FIPS - STATE - ST_ABBR - COUNTY - LOCATION - POPCHANGE - dem_pct - oth_pct - rep_pct - DEMOCRAT - OTHER - REPUBLICAN - total_turnout - Male_percentage_estimate, data = data, kernel = "radial", scale = FALSE) # use radial kernel because data is not linearly separable
summary(svm_fit)
```

```{r}
svm_pred <- predict(svm_fit, data)
confusion <- confusionMatrix(svm_pred, data$highest_party)
print(confusion)
```
